correctness.rationale: When the unique vacancy lies in the a-part, a mixed b-part gives red and blue no-improvement inequalities (b-1)x <= (a-1)(y-1) and (a-1)y <= (b-1)x, which cannot hold simultaneously; a monochromatic b-part makes all jumps non-improving. Symmetry gives the complete converse, four disjoint cases yield the binomial count, the near-balanced count is 2m, and the K_{a,2} equilibria have exactly two welfare values a+1 and 2+4/(a-1). The exact minimum and universal maximum give PoA (a-1)/2. Standalone brute rational-payoff tests covered 15136 assignments in 80 parameter classes, and the balanced and price-of-anarchy families. Finite tests do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The classification resolves every equilibrium configuration and its exact labeled multiplicity on a canonical family, exposing two mathematically opposite regimes. In balanced bicliques equilibrium is exponentially rare but always socially optimal. Conversely, in K_{a,2} with two minority agents, almost all equilibria are inefficient and the sharp price of anarchy grows like a/2 despite diameter two, vertex-connectivity two and no leaves. The latter strengthens the qualitative setting of the published star lower-bound example, giving a motivated structural boundary rather than an arbitrary small finite census.
